sn35.121:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Savatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anathapiṇḍika’s Park.
sn35.121:1.2: Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in his mind thus:
sn35.121:1.3: “The states that ripen in liberation have come to maturity in Rahula.
sn35.121:1.4: Let me lead him on further to the destruction of the taints.”
sn35.121:1.5: Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed and, taking bowl and robe, walked for alms in Savatthī.
sn35.121:1.6: When he had returned from the alms round, after his meal he addressed the Venerable Rahula thus:
sn35.121:1.8: Let us go to the Blind Men’s Grove for the day’s abiding.”
sn35.121:1.9: “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Rahula replied and, having taken a sitting cloth, he followed close behind the Blessed One.
sn35.121:2.1: Now on that occasion many thousands of devatās followed the Blessed One, thinking:
sn35.121:2.2: “Today the Blessed One will lead the Venerable Rahula on further to the destruction of the taints.”
sn35.121:2.3: Then the Blessed One plunged into the Blind Men’s Grove and sat down at the foot of a certain tree on a seat that was prepared for him.
sn35.121:2.4: The Venerable Rahula paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
sn35.121:2.5: The Blessed One then said to him:
sn35.121:3.2: is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
sn35.121:5.1: “Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?”–
sn35.121:7.1: “Is what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
sn35.121:7.2: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”–
sn35.121:15.1: Is anything included in feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness arisen with eye-contact as condition permanent or impermanent?”–
sn35.121:19.2: The rest as in the preceding paragraph.
sn35.121:45.1: Is anything included in feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness arisen with mind-contact as condition permanent or impermanent?”–
sn35.121:47.1: “Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?”–
sn35.121:49.1: “Is what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
sn35.121:49.2: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”–
sn35.121:51.1: “Seeing thus, Rahula, the instructed noble disciple experiences revulsion towards the eye, revulsion towards forms, revulsion towards eye-consciousness, revulsion towards eye-contact; revulsion towards anything included in feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness arisen with eye-contact as condition.
sn35.121:51.2: He experiences revulsion towards the ear …
sn35.121:52.1: towards the mind … towards anything included in feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness arisen with mind-contact as condition.
sn35.121:52.2: “Experiencing revulsion, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion his mind is liberated. When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated.’
sn35.121:52.3: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”
sn35.121:53.1: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn35.121:53.2: Elated, the Venerable Rahula delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.
sn35.121:53.3: And while this discourse was being spoken, the Venerable Rahula’s mind was liberated from the taints by nonclinging,
sn35.121:53.4: and in those many thousands of devatās there arose the dust-free, stainless vision of the Dhamma:
sn35.121:53.5: “Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation.”
